name: Kabras
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Möhlig 1985 (Bantu dialectology) and Odden 2009 cited for subclassification; no phonological description of Kabras stress located.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference export for kabr1240 (4 refs: Ebarb 2016; Kanyoro 1983; ISO 639-3 change request 2007-171; Huntingford, Ghosts and devils in East Africa)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; the sole phonological work listed is Ebarb 2016.

sources.citation: Mudogo, Maxmillah. 2025. Morpho-phonological adaptation of verb borrowings from English on the vitality of Lukabras language. MA thesis, Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST). 122 pp.
sources.note: No placement statement. One generic remark (p. 54) that epenthetic /i/ 'aids in proper word stress and rhythm'. Claims (pp. 59-60) that Lukabras has no long vowels, which conflicts with Ebarb & Marlo's Luyia vowel-length work; treated as unreliable.

sources.citation: Chenenje, Solomon Luvonga. 2024. Phonological basis of mispronunciation in spoken English of Kabarasi people in social setting. Journal of Linguistics, Literature and Language Teaching (JLLLT) 3(2): 60-69. doi:10.37249/jlllt.v3i2.704
sources.note: Explicitly did not treat it: p. 68 'The researcher did not manage to analyze the diacritics, stress, and intonation due to time factors'. Gives a 45-item Kabras wordlist with impressionistic transcriptions (long vowels marked in some penults/antepenults) and a consonant chart; states (p. 63) that per Ebarb 2016 Kabras is undocumented apart from Ebarb's own work.

sources.citation: Lukania, Valentine Robai. 2024. Morpho-pragmatic analysis of Lukabarasi nominal compounds. MA thesis, MMUST. 119 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the only 'stress' hits are in quoted theory about German compounds and a Lexical Phonology diagram). Notes that the final element of a Lukabarasi nominal compound ends in a high tone (compound prosody), i.e. treats the language as tonal.

sources.citation: Osotsi, Eric M. 2020. A systematic reconstruction of the phonology of Proto-Luyia: a comparative analysis. MA thesis, University of Nairobi. 127 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent; segmental reconstruction from seven Luyia varieties that do not include Kabras (Kabras only named in the classification, p. 12 and p. 14).

sources.citation: Sasala, James Matseshe. 2020. Lexical borrowing in spoken Lukabaras from the Nandi language in Chepsaita Scheme, Uasin Gishu County, Kenya. MA thesis, MMUST. 107 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Five-vowel inventory and phonotactics (no word-final consonants) cited from Mukulo 2016; no suprasegmentals.

sources.citation: Wasitia, James Indimuli. 2005. An investigation into the absence of voiced stop and fricative sounds in Kabarasi. MA dissertation, University of Nairobi, Department of Linguistics and African Languages. 81 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Consonant inventory and stop/fricative processes only (grep for stress/accent/penult/tone/length: only the word 'accent' inside a quoted statement of Verner's law, p. 8). No suprasegmental section.

sources.citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J. 2016. An overview of Kabarasi verb tone. Language 92(3): e134-e191.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: The only professional phonological description of Kabarasi; its preliminaries section (vowel length, tone-bearing units, phrase-penultimate phenomena) is the most likely place for any statement on stress or its absence.

sources.citation: Mukulo, K. 2016. Phonological adaptation of English loanwords in Lukabras. MA thesis, Moi University, Eldoret.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Cited by Sasala 2020 and Mudogo 2025 as the source for Lukabras phonotactics and vowel inventory; a loanword-adaptation thesis often contains a stress/tone adaptation section.

sources.citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J. & Michael R. Marlo. 2015. Vowel length sensitivity in Luyia morphophonology. Southern African Linguistics and Applied Language Studies 33(3): 373-390.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Deals with vowel length across Luyia varieties including Kabarasi; the natural place for any statement on penultimate lengthening (the usual 'stress' correlate in Luyia).

sources.citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J. 2014. Tone and variation in Idakho and other Luhya varieties. PhD dissertation, Indiana University, Bloomington.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Ebarb's dissertation is the source Ebarb 2016 builds on and compares Kabarasi with other Luyia varieties; likely to contain remarks on prosody/penultimate lengthening across Luyia.

sources.citation: Ebarb, Kristopher J., Christopher R. Green & Michael R. Marlo. 2014. Luyia tone melodies. Africana Linguistica 20: 121-143.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not fetched sources
sources.note: Open on Persée in principle; surveys Luyia tone systems incl. Kabarasi and may state that Luyia varieties are tonal without stress or note penultimate lengthening.

sources.citation: Kanyoro, Rachel Angogo. 1983. Unity in diversity: a linguistic survey of the Abaluyia of western Kenya. Wien: Afro-Pub (Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 20). 322 pp. (Revision of her 1980 University of Texas at Austin dissertation.)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Comparative phonology of 18 Luyia varieties including Kabras; the earliest source with Kabras data and possibly a general remark on Luyia stress/tone.

sources.citation: Katui. 2025. Phonological basis of mispronunciation in spoken Swahili of Kabarasi speaking students in secondary schools of Kakamega North Sub-County. Journal of Languages and Linguistics 4(1). doi:10.51317/jll.v4i1.778
sources.note: Landing page only; the journal's PDF galley returned HTTP 500 on three attempts. Same genre as Chenenje 2024, so unlikely to state stress placement.
